The “X” needs to be removed. The “X” in the top corner of the app needs to be removed. 
When you click on it it closes the bible entirely and you have to open it back up and try and find your spot again. 
Its placement in the top left corner causes me to close out where I am at and I have to start over again. 
Why? Example, I’m reading through a passage and I click on the word to see what the Strongs says about it. When I’m done I want to get out of that window and back onto the passage I was reading. In many popular apps out there to close a pop up window and get back to the previous screen you go up to the top left or right and click an “X” to close that window and you are back to what you were just looking at. 

In this app however that “X” closes everything and there is no way to get back to where you were, it’s highly frustrating.

reviews.text:
Best app for Bible readers!. I hardly ever leave a review, but this app has been so helpful for me in digging deeper into the Word. I mainly use it for the Interlinear, parallel with Greek or Hebrew, and Commentary. I’m adding the Cross Reference feature to that list as of today! I love being able to learn the original text and the truer meaning by clicking on a word without having gone to seminary. I LOVE that they added the historical context for what words mean and how they were used in societies. I also love how they have Greek/Hebrew parallels in the definitions so I don’t have to hunt the internet for what the equivalents would be.

Only things I’d want to have upgraded are:
• like YouVersion, having a free account to highlight, save, and bookmark what I’d like to go back to
• I’d make the interface more like an app than the safari browser it is, possibly survey millennials and gen z what we’d like in an upgraded interface
• a clearer means of interpreting Hebrew definitions for lay people without losing the essence old what is laid out, perhaps a symbols and shorthand key at the bottom of a word definition page that lists what’s used on that page and their meanings. I know Hebrew is what theology majors at my Bible college used to say was so darn hard, and I’m seeing why

As for the review that was upset about there being versions on here that remove certain things, I actually think it’s wise because they are surrounded by tons of resources. They aren’t stand alone and the only versions available. This will also help people in their exploration through the app learn of other versions, notice that things are missing in certain versions, and grow in their curiosity about how different versions and transliterations came to be and why.

I’m still exploring what other features do what, but I’ve been using this app for almost a year and it’s a winner for me!! Us lay people thank you for both the website and app!
